answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybils by making identity expensive: each agent locks a deposit that vests slowly, so creating many fake agents multiplies the locked capital rather than the influence. The delta between an agent's earned fees and its staked bond is published, letting peers price trust; a mesa of accumulated honest work raises the bond's yield, while a fresh knoll of a newcomer earns almost nothing until it survives audits. Cheating triggers slashing of the whole bond, so an attacker must pay full price for every identity it fakes.
